name: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: Choosing appropriate data structures and algorithms and reasoning about their time and space complexity.

resources.title: VisuAlgo: visualising data structures and algorithms

questions.question: Which data structure follows Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order?
questions.explanation: A stack removes the most recently added element first (push/pop at the same end).

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the remaining search range, so at most about log2(n) comparisons are needed.

questions.question: What is the average-case time complexity of looking up a key in a well-implemented hash table?
questions.explanation: With a good hash function and resizing, lookups take constant time on average; collisions only degrade the worst case.

questions.question: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending sorted order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits left subtree, node, then right subtree, which yields BST keys in sorted order.

questions.question: Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm is not guaranteed to produce correct results when the graph contains:
questions.explanation: Dijkstra assumes a finalised node's distance can never decrease, which negative edges violate; Bellman-Ford handles them.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of quicksort that always picks the first element as pivot when run on an already sorted array?
questions.explanation: Each partition peels off only one element, giving n levels of O(n) work, i.e. O(n^2).

practical.title: Detect duplicates in linear time
practical.instructions: Write a Python function has_duplicate(nums) that returns True if any value appears more than once in the list and False otherwise. It must run in O(n) time. After the code, state its time complexity in one line.
practical.expected_output: A function that tracks seen values in a set (or compares len(set(nums)) to len(nums)), returns True/False, and states the complexity is O(n).

rubric.description: Uses a set for O(1) membership
rubric.hint: A set gives constant-time membership checks; a nested loop is O(n^2).
Check 'if x in seen' or compare len(set(nums)) with len(nums).
Return True when a duplicate is found, False otherwise.
State the complexity explicitly, e.g. 'Time: O(n)'.

tasks.title: Learn Big-O and core data structures
tasks.description: Study asymptotic notation, binary search and selection/insertion sort on Khan Academy. Write a one-line Big-O summary for arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues and hash tables.
tasks.completion_criteria: A summary table of access/search/insert complexity for 5 data structures.

tasks.title: Implement basic structures from scratch
tasks.description: Implement a stack, a queue and a singly linked list in Python with push/pop, enqueue/dequeue and insert/delete. Use VisuAlgo to compare your mental model with the animations.
tasks.completion_criteria: Three classes with working operations verified by small test cases.

tasks.title: Solve problems with trees, graphs and hashing
tasks.description: Solve 10 problems covering hash maps, BST traversal, BFS/DFS on graphs and two-pointer techniques. For each, write down the time and space complexity before coding.
tasks.completion_criteria: 10 accepted solutions with complexity noted for each.

tasks.title: Build a route finder
tasks.description: Build a small program that loads a weighted graph (e.g. city distances) from a file and finds shortest paths with Dijkstra's algorithm using a heap. Compare its runtime against a naive approach on a larger generated graph.
tasks.completion_criteria: Program returns correct shortest paths on test graphs and includes a short runtime comparison.
